Calculation Details

MetricValueNote

How to estimate trip fuel cost

Choose US or metric units, enter one-way distance, select one way or round trip, then add your vehicle's real-world fuel economy and expected pump price. Multiple trips and cost sharing are included.

US fuel cost = total miles / MPG x price per gallon

Metric fuel cost = total kilometers x L/100 km / 100 x price per liter

Road-trip example

A 650-mile one-way trip in a 28 MPG vehicle uses about 23.21 US gallons. At $3.60 per gallon, estimated fuel cost is $83.57. A round trip doubles distance, fuel, and cost before any extra detours.

Plan a more realistic fuel budget

Use your recent highway or mixed-driving average rather than the best published rating. Add expected detour mileage to the distance field and use an average fuel price for the route. When you need an official model estimate, check fueleconomy.gov. The result excludes tolls, parking, maintenance, depreciation, lodging, and food.

Splitting gas money

The per-person result divides fuel cost evenly by the number of travelers. It does not assign different shares for the driver, vehicle owner, or passengers, so adjust the entered count or agree on a different split when needed.

US and metric modes

US mode uses miles, MPG, and price per US gallon. Metric mode uses kilometers, L/100 km, and price per liter. Currency selection changes display only; it does not perform an exchange-rate conversion.

Frequently asked questions

Should distance be one way?

Yes. Enter one-way distance and choose Round trip when you plan to return over roughly the same distance.

Where can I find my vehicle's MPG?

Use a recent fill-to-fill calculation for the most relevant estimate, or start with the combined rating for the exact vehicle configuration.

Does the result include idling?

Only indirectly if your entered real-world MPG already reflects idling. Add a margin for heavy traffic, cold weather, towing, or long stationary periods.
